source.title: Beyond What to Select: A Plug-and-play Oscillatory Data-Volume Scheduling for Efficient Model Training
source.authors: Suorong Yang; Han Zhu; Hai-Xiang Gan; Fang-Yi Su; Guang Li; Fu-Rao Shen; Soujanya Poria

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains models on selected subsets of natural-label data and reports held-out benchmark performance, testing how a different training-data schedule affects generalization. It does not test random-label memorization or the specific interventions and measurements in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: Results bear on natural-label held-out performance under data selection and scheduling. The paper does not report training error alongside test error, so these results do not quantify the train–test gap. Cited results from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Table 8 tests the optimizer-performance component of V4 in a data-volume scheduling setting: Adam has lower CIFAR-10 accuracy than SGD at every reported budget. The tuning protocol is unspecified, so the limited-tuning condition cannot be verified. The extracted rows themselves test none of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that oscillatory data-volume scheduling exploits selection-induced regularization while preserving optimization stability and improving training efficiency across tasks. Their cross-optimizer conclusion concerns PODS compatibility, although Table 8 also permits optimizer-performance comparisons.
record.recipe_differences: The study schedules the volume of selected natural-label training data under a cumulative budget; it does not use the original claim's random-label, width, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports performance across selection ratios and datasets, architectures, and tasks; its ablation varies oscillation margin ϵ and states that larger values slightly reduce accuracy. These are data-selection schedule conditions, not tests of V1–V8.

fits_no_version.finding: PODS improves ImageNet accuracy from 76.4% to 76.8% at a 60% cumulative data budget, matches the displayed instruction-tuning averages at 50%, and improves reasoning averages under equal optimization steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Oscillatory data-volume scheduling can preserve or improve held-out performance with reduced data exposure in the reported settings.

record.problems: No training-error measurements are reported, so the train–test gap cannot be assessed directly. The text reports no uncertainty estimates. Some performance comparisons are figures or flattened tables; those results are not reconstructed here.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted Table 1 comparisons because the flattened table does not reliably assign all values to methods and selection ratios. Omitted Tables 3–4, Figures 3–4, and Tables 7–10: they concern long-tailed/OOD outcomes, detection, compatibility, optimizer accuracy, or ablations and do not test any listed version; some are figure-only or flattened. Cited prior-work findings were excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
The limited-tuning condition, broader tuning, training-performance comparisons, language benchmarks, decoupled weight decay and optimizer switching.
Batch-size variation under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to large batches.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization gaps and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence versus removing equally many random examples.

missing.what: Add optimizer-specific accuracy rows and SGD comparisons at each budget. Although rows_left_out declares Table 8 omitted, its assertion that these results bear on no version is incorrect.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of training-error measurements does not prevent a held-out optimizer comparison for V4. It does prevent evaluating its training-performance component. Table 2's reduction from 140 to 84 GPU hours is 40%, despite the abstract and introduction claiming 50% savings.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fit random labels or compare their held-out performance with natural-label performance.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD under the tuning conditions in the version.
Does not vary batch size or test a large-batch generalization penalty.
Does not measure sharpness or compare generalization measures.
Does not identify or remove memorized examples.
